body.statement: Suppose \(\delta_0<1/2\) and \(B^4>(Sd)^2\).  There are constants \(c_0>0\) and \(\eta_0>0\), depending only on fixed class parameters, such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the base Holder model class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) contains two laws whose realized interior paths are separated by order \(N^{-1/2}\), whose observed-data total variation distance is at most \(1-\eta_0\), and whose causal targets are separated by at least \(c_0N^{-\kappa/2}\).  The training and treated-event observed laws can be chosen identical; only the donor-location experiment and the transported untreated potential mean differ.  No lower local-modulus condition is used.
body.justification: A common-support three-point donor location family and an affine or cusp regression certify the donor lower rate while the donor sample is constructed independently of the entire common observed panel.
body.gap: At the Jensen-minimal fourth-moment boundary the donor law may be singular, so strict moment slack is genuinely required.
body.consumer: The marginal MSE and honest-length converses use this regular overlapping family.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(q=Sd\) and \(\Delta_B=B^4-q^2>0\).  Choose \(a_D>1\) so that
\[
 1<a_D^2<1+\Delta_B/2.                                            \tag{1}
\]
For \(|u|\) in a sufficiently small fixed neighborhood of zero, define
\(V_u\in\{-a_D,0,a_D\}\) by
\[
 p_+(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}+\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_-(u)=\frac{1+u^2}{2a_D^2}-\frac{u}{2a_D},\quad
 p_0(u)=1-\frac{1+u^2}{a_D^2}.                                   \tag{2}
\]
The probabilities are positive after shrinking the neighborhood, and direct
summation gives
\[
 \mathbb EV_u=u,\qquad\operatorname{Var}(V_u)=1.                  \tag{3}
\]
Let the other \(q-1\) coordinates be independent Rademacher variables.  At
\(u=0\),
\[
 \mathbb E\|V_0^{(q)}\|_2^4
 =a_D^2+2(q-1)+(q-1)^2=q^2-1+a_D^2<B^4.                           \tag{4}
\]
The centered fourth moment is continuous in \(u\), so the strict bound
persists on a smaller fixed neighborhood.

Put \(z^{(0)}=\tfrac12\mathbf1_q\) and
\(z^{(1)}=z^{(0)}+\delta_Ne_1\), where
\(\delta_N=c_*N^{-1/2}\).  Since \(\delta_0<1/2\), both paths are
interior for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Under alternative
\(v\in\{0,1\}\), take i.i.d. donors whose first coordinate is
\(1/2+V_{v\delta_N}\) and whose remaining coordinates are \(1/2\) plus the
common Rademacher coordinates.  Then
\[
 \mathbb E_vZ_j=z^{(v)},\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_v(Z_j)=I_q,\qquad
 \mathbb E_v\|Z_j-z^{(v)}\|_2^4\le B^4.                           \tag{5}
\]
Because \(c_\Sigma\le1\le C_\Sigma\), the full covariance is uniformly
elliptic.

The square roots of the three probabilities in (2) have bounded second
derivatives near zero, their affinity equals one at zero, and its first
derivative is zero.  Thus the one-donor Hellinger affinity is at least
\(1-C_0\delta_N^2\).  Product factorization and the Cauchy--Schwarz
total-variation inequality give
\[
 \|P_1^{Z,N}-P_0^{Z,N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\{1-(1-C_0\delta_N^2)^{2N}\}^{1/2}.                           \tag{6}
\]
Choosing fixed \(c_*>0\) sufficiently small makes (6) at most
\(1-\eta_0\) for some fixed \(\eta_0>0\).

Use a common i.i.d. uniform exact training design.  If
\(0<\kappa<1\), set
\[
 m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)_+^\kappa;
\]
if \(\kappa=1\), use the affine function
\(m_1(x)=b_0+b_1(x_1-1/2)\).  Set all other surfaces equal to \(b_0\).
For \(\lambda<1\), \(\kappa=\lambda\) and the positive-part power is
\(\lambda\)-Holder.  For \(\lambda\ge1\), the affine surface belongs to
every stated Holder class.  Sufficiently small positive \(b_0,b_1\), chosen
in terms of \(B,L\), enforce the Holder radius and boundedness, and
\[
 |m_1(z^{(1)}_1)-m_1(z^{(0)}_1)|=b_1\delta_N^\kappa.               \tag{7}
\]
Use identical bounded centered training noise, the same training design,
and identical positive constant treated observations under both laws.  Set
\(B_{si}(1)=B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) and the unobserved untreated event wealth
to \(m_s(z_s^{(v)})\).  Taking \(W_{si,-1}=1\),
\(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\) realizes
these wealth levels under \texttt{def:buyhold-level}.

We verify membership.  The uniform design has conditional density one
Lebesgue-almost everywhere, uniformly over dates and cohorts, and its
conditional beta-mixing coefficients are zero.  Thus the corrected
\texttt{ass:design-density} and \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} hold at the
constant query under each law.  The constructions above verify boundedness,
Holder smoothness, consistency, event-date transport, and conditional
centering.  Unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\), while arbitrary
dependence inside each chosen history is allowed.  The donor primitive is
independent of the design, all training responses, and all treated outcomes,
so \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} holds for the complete joint
panel.  Donor independence, unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the fourth-moment
bound follow from (5).  Hence both laws are in
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

The observed panel factors are identical and (6) controls the only differing
observed factor.  Lemma \texttt{lem:causal-identification} and (7) give
\[
 |\tau_1(z^{(1)})-\tau_0(z^{(0)})|
 =\pi_1b_1c_*^\kappa N^{-\kappa/2}.                               \tag{8}
\]
This proves the two-law certificate without a class-wide lower local
modulus.
